To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) tensegrity structures are a viable option for robotic joints; (2) tensegrity joints have the ability to handle off-axis moments without compromising their structural stability; (3) tensegrity manipulators can have a large number of passive degrees of freedom; and (4) tensegrity robots are lightweight, compact, and can be used in a variety of applications.

(i) the proposed tensegrity structures are lightweight, modular, bio-inspired robotic arms with multi-degree of freedom, structurally compliant, and active joints; (ii) the joints are able to passively and robustly handle off-axis moments and large deformations; and (iii) the proposed structures can be used to design robotic arms with multiple degrees of freedom and active joints.
